messages.text:
Short version: the server controls the **content** you see on the glasses. The app controls the **chrome** around it: buttons, recording, layout. I checked the server code for any flags it could send to switch app features on or off, and there aren't any.

**Things the server can control**, because it sends them as data:
- **Text:** Claude's streamed reply, the tool lines (name and summary), the final result text.
- **Permission prompts:** the description, the detail line, and the wording and number of the choices ("Yes" / "Yes, and always…" / "No").
- **Question cards:** the question text and the options.
- **Notifications:** the title and the message.
- **Session list:** the titles, and the account, model and version shown from `/api/info`.
- **Status signals:** busy/idle, thinking started/ended, text started/ended. These drive the app's indicators, and the server can choose not to send them.
- **Progress:** elapsed time and tokens, and to-do progress like "3/7 · current task".
- **What happens behind the buttons:** "Stop" calls the server's interrupt endpoint, and the server decides what interrupting means.

**Things the server can't control** (the app's own UI):
- **The Stop button itself:** the server can't hide or rename it.
- **"Release to finish recording":** the whole voice flow is the app's, including recording, speech-to-text and that prompt. The server only receives the finished text.
- **Fonts, text size, layout, scrolling, menus**, and how each kind of event is drawn.
- **New buttons or screens.** An event type the app doesn't recognise is probably just ignored, but I haven't checked that.

**Unknown until we test on the glasses:** how the app uses some fields it receives. Examples are whether it shows the full tool output or only the summary, whether it shows cost, and whether a tool's "finished" line replaces its "started" line.

The cleanest way to settle all of that is a small display probe in our fork: a test endpoint that sends one of each event …[truncated 290 chars]

Well, I have a better idea: why don't we rewrite the event server from scratch?I don't know in what language.I sure hope not JavaScript.Maybe something more appropriate for network stuff.Maybe Go?I mean, maybe Rust?I don't know what the agent SDK is more comfortable talking to.I don't know.I kind of hope this would be like a standalone binary we could release for, you know.ux and Windows, so that you don't have to set up a Python environment or worse.NPM or NPX, terrible stuff.So give me some ideas.
